# Things you can say

<!-- Generated by scripts/gen-commands-doc.mjs from the command grammar and its tests; edit those, then run it again. -->

Everything on this page works **without an AI brain**, on your computer, in a few milliseconds. Say it the way you normally would: Dayspring ignores "um", "please", "could you" and "hey Dayspring", understands numbers said as words ("twenty five"), and fixes common mishearings ("set a time her"). Every example here is checked by the automated tests on every build.

**Ending the conversation** and **Stop** (below) are in every version since 1.7.3 (Settings → This app → Features: **Stop and goodbye**). The rest of these commands are new in the development version (1.8.0), listed there as **Everyday commands without AI**. A reminder at a clock time (“remind me to drink water at 11pm”) works in every version. For the full list of everyday requests (timers, the Bible, recipes, math and more), see [Using Dayspring without AI](using-without-ai.md).

## Ending the conversation

When you're done, just say so. Dayspring answers briefly and stops listening right away, instead of waiting for more. Tacked onto a request ("set a timer for 5 minutes, thanks"), it does the request and asks no follow-up question.

- Thanks: “Thanks” · “Thank you” · “Thank you so much” · “Thanks a lot” · “Thanks dayspring” · “Thank you very much”
- Done: “That's all” · “That's it” · “That'll be all” · “That will be all” · “Nothing else” · “Nothing more” · “No that's fine” · “No that's it”
- Goodbye: “Goodbye” · “Bye” · “Bye bye” · “See you” · “See you later” · “See ya” · “Good night” · “Goodnight” · “Night night”
- Never mind: “Never mind” · “Nevermind” · “Forget it”
- On the end of a request: “Set a timer for 5 minutes thanks” · “Set a timer for 5 minutes, thank you” · “What time is it thanks”
- Not an ending: "thanks for the reminder, now set a timer for 10 minutes" sets the timer; "never mind the timer, cancel it" cancels it; "remind me to say thank you at 5" is a reminder.

If Dayspring just asked you something, "no thanks" or "that's all" answers it (nothing happens) and ends the conversation.

### Stop

Say **"stop"**, "that's enough", "enough", "shh", "hush", "be quiet", "cancel", "never mind", "okay that's good" or "got it, thanks" on its own, even while Dayspring is talking, and it stops right away: mid-sentence, the rest of the reply, a document being read aloud, and any question it was asking. It doesn't say "okay, stopping". Only this conversation ends: Dayspring keeps listening for its name, so the next "Dayspring, …" works at once. (✋ Stop, the mic button, "stop listening" and "go to sleep" are what stop listening altogether.)

Music and videos keep playing when you stop Dayspring's voice. A plain "Dayspring, stop" while nothing is being said stops the music; "stop the music", "stop the timer" and "stop the alarm" always mean just that.

## Every setting

Any setting can be changed and asked about by voice: turn it on or off, set a value, make it bigger or smaller, louder or quieter, reset it, or ask what it's set to. Dayspring always says what changed. **"Undo that"** puts the last change back.

|---|---|

| For a while, then back by itself | “Make it rain for 10 minutes” · “Let it rain for an hour” · “Make it snow for half an hour” · “Make it night for an hour” |
| Time of day | “Make it night” · “Make it sunset” · “Make it sunrise” · “Make it noon” · “Make it dusk” · “Make it golden hour” |

| Season | “Make it winter” · “Make it fall” · “Make it spring” |
| A whole look | “Cozy vibe” · “Calm vibe” · “Vivid mode” · “Make the background warmer” · “Make the background darker” · “Make the sky brighter” |
| The window | “Compact mode” · “Full screen” · “Exit full screen” |

Add "for 10 minutes" (or "for an hour") to any sky change and it goes back by itself. The scenery Dayspring has is hills, fields, forest and river; for anything else ("mountains", "the beach") it picks the closest and tells you.

## Your schedule, with repeats

- Add: “Schedule a dentist appointment next Tuesday at 3” · “Add gym every Monday Wednesday Friday at 6am for an hour” · “Bible study every weeknight at 9” · “Add team sync the first Monday of every month at 10” · “Schedule a review on the last friday of every month at 3pm” · “Add piano on the 15th of each month at 4pm”
- Move: “Move my 3pm to 4” · “Move it to 5” · “Make it 6pm instead” · “Move the dentist to 4pm” · “Push the meeting to thursday”
- Cancel one, or a day of a repeating one: “Cancel Friday's gym” · “Skip gym tomorrow” · “Cancel my 3pm” · “Cancel the dentist” · “Cancel my dentist appointment”
- Make it repeat, or change how often: “Make it recurring” · “Make it weekly” · “Change it to every two weeks” · “Make gym repeat every monday” · “Change bible study to mondays and wednesdays”
- Stop repeating: “Stop repeating” · “Cancel all gym” · “Stop repeating it” · “Stop gym for good”

How often: every day, weekdays, weekends, weeknights (Monday to Friday), every Monday Wednesday and Friday, every other week (or every other Friday), every 3 weeks, the first Monday of every month, the last Friday of the month, the 15th of each month, every year; with "until December" (through November 30), "until December 15", "for the next 3 weeks", "starting next Monday", "except holidays" (US federal holidays) or "every day except Sunday".

When: today, tonight, tomorrow, this weekend (Saturday), next Tuesday, in 3 days, next month on the 5th, October 12th, at noon, half past 6, quarter to 9, from 3 to 5, for an hour. Times of day on their own:

| Said | Means |
|---|---|
| first thing | 8 a.m. |
| morning | 9 a.m. |
| noon | 12 p.m. |
| lunch | 12 p.m. |
| lunchtime | 12 p.m. |
| afternoon | 2 p.m. |
| after work | 5:30 p.m. |
| evening | 6 p.m. |
| dinner | 6 p.m. |
| dinnertime | 6 p.m. |
| tonight | 8 p.m. |
| night | 8 p.m. |
| bedtime | 9:30 p.m. |

A bare hour from 1 to 6 means p.m. and 7 to 11 means a.m., unless the words say otherwise ("at 9 tonight", "every weeknight at 9" → 9 p.m.). For a one-time item with no day, it's whichever comes next. For a repeating one at 7 to 11 with no a.m. or p.m., Dayspring asks once.

## Reminders

- Once, at a time: “Remind me to drink water at 11pm” · “Remind me to drink water at 11 tonight” · “Remind me to drink water at 7:30” · “Remind me to drink water tomorrow at 6am” · “Remind me to call mom tomorrow at 6pm” (today, or tomorrow once the time has passed; never every hour)
- Repeating: “Remind me to take out the trash every Thursday night” · “Remind me to pay rent on the 1st of every month at 9am” · “Remind me to pay rent on the 15th of each month” · “Remind me to drink water every day at 11pm” · “Remind me to take my pills every morning at 8”
- Every few minutes: “Every 30 minutes remind me to stand up” · “Remind me to stretch every hour” · “Remind me to drink water every hour” · “Remind me to drink water every 30 minutes”
- Stop: “Stop reminding me to stand up” · “Stop reminding me to stretch” · “Stop the stand up reminders” · “Don't remind me to call mom” · “Don't remind me”

## Timers and alarms

- A timer until a clock time: “Set a timer for 7:45” · “Set a timer until 5 pm” · “Timer till 3:30” · “Set a timer until noon”
- Alarms: “A timer that goes off every day at 7” · “Set an alarm for weekdays at 6:30” · “Set an alarm for Saturday at 8” · “Set an alarm for 8 on weekends” · “Wake me up at 6 every weekday” · “Set an alarm for 7am” · “Wake me up at 6:30 tomorrow” · “Set a gentle alarm for 6 with the bells” · “Set a loud alarm for 5:30 called gym with a 5 minute snooze” · “Set an alarm for 7 that flashes the screen”
- What's set: “What alarms do I have” · “List my alarms” · “Show my alarms” · “What alarms are set”
- Off and on (kept for later): “Turn off my weekend alarms” · “Turn my weekend alarms back on” · “Turn off my weekday alarms” · “Turn off the 6:30 alarm”
- Skip a day: “Skip tomorrow's alarm” · “Skip saturday's alarm” · “Skip the next alarm” · “Skip my alarm tomorrow”
- Change or delete: “Change my 6:30 alarm to 6:45” · “Make the alarm loud” · “Make my alarm gentle” · “Delete the 6:30 alarm” · “Delete the gym alarm” · “Delete all my alarms”

An alarm can have a label ("called gym"), a sound (bells, chimes, birds, beeps, soft, fanfare), a volume ("loud", "quiet", "at 60 percent"), a snooze length ("with a 5 minute snooze"), a gentle wake (starts soft and builds over three minutes) and a flashing screen ("flash the screen", "vibrate"). A bare hour from 4 to 10 is in the morning, and so is any repeating alarm. Alarms still ring when the Dayspring window is closed.

Plain timers ("set a timer for 10 minutes", "pause the pasta timer", "add 5 minutes", "how long is left on the laundry") work as always: up to 7 at once, each with a name.

## You

- Your name: “My name is Morgan” · “Call me Robin” · “I go by Z” · “My name's Morgan” · “Add a nickname Ziggy” · “Remove the nickname Ziggy” · “What's my name?” · “What is my name”
- Where you live: “I live in Springfield, Illinois” · “Set my location to Peoria” · “My zip code is 62701” · “I moved to Decatur” · “Where do you think I am?” · “Where am i”
- About you: “I'm a carpenter” · “I'm a teacher” · “I work at Acme Tools” · “My birthday is July 9th” · “My birthday's july 9th”
- What you like: “I like kayaking and D&D” · “Add fishing to my interests” · “Remove D&D from my interests” · “I love kayaking and d&d” · “I don't like country music” · “I do not like country music”
- Looking back: “What do you know about me?” · “What are my interests” · “What am i interested in” · “Forget that I like country music” · “Forget that I'm a carpenter”
- All of it, one question at a time: “Let me tell you about myself” · “I want to tell you about myself” · “Get to know me” (say "skip" to skip one, "stop" or "that's all" to finish)

"My name is" is you; "your name is" is Dayspring's own name (see [Personality](personality.md)). "I live in" and "I moved to" change where you are; "I'm going to Chicago tomorrow" doesn't. Your town is looked up online once (the same way as Settings → Where you are); everything else stays on this computer.

## Two at once, and changing your mind

- Two requests: “Turn off the lights and set a timer for 10 minutes” · “Turn off the weather and make it rain” · “Set the volume to 40 and use 24 hour time” · “Make it snow and hide the clock”
- The last thing: “Move it to 5” · “Move it to 5pm” · “Make it 5”
- Corrections: “Not tomorrow, friday” · “No, not at 5, at 6” · “I said 6pm” · “No not tomorrow friday”
- Changed your mind: “Undo” · “Undo that” · “Undo it” · “Undo the last change” · “Don't set a timer” · “Don't add that”

When something important is missing ("schedule a haircut" with no day or time), Dayspring asks one question. Say "never mind" to drop it.
